articles.title: Com mercado em alta, procura por cursos de tecnologia da Unesp cresce  | G1
articles.standfirst: Procura por graduações ligadas à tecnologia da informação acompanha expansão da inteligência artificial. Primeira fase do vestibular da Unesp é no dia 22 de novembro.
articles.summary: Procura por graduações ligadas à tecnologia da informação acompanha expansão da inteligência artificial. Primeira fase do vestibular da Unesp é no dia 22 de novembro.
articles.body:
Unesp 2027: Cursos de tecnologia ganham cada vez mais espaço entre os vestibulandos — Foto: Acervo

Impulsionados pela expansão do mercado de tecnologia e pelo avanço da inteligência artificial (IA), os cursos ligados à tecnologia da informação (TI) estão entre os mais procurados na Universidade Estadual Paulista ( Unesp ).

Dados da Vunesp mostram que a relação candidato por vaga vem crescendo desde 2017. Em ciência da computação, a concorrência aumentou até 52% em Rio Claro (SP).

🔎 A Unesp registrou 65.706 inscritos no vestibular 2027 . Os candidatos disputam 5.850 vagas distribuídas em 137 cursos de graduação de 24 cidades do estado de São Paulo. Confira aqui estatística de inscritos por curso.

📚 Esta reportagem compõe o projeto Vestibulou, uma iniciativa do g1 São Carlos e Araraquara para divulgar informações relacionadas aos principais vestibulares e ajudar na preparação dos estudantes.

De acordo com o coordenador do curso de bacharelado em ciências da computação da Unesp de São José do Rio Preto , Rodrigo Capobianco Guido, um "avanço vertiginoso dos sistemas de inteligência artificial (IA)" também tem impulsionado a procura pelos cursos de graduação.

Além da IA, o coordenador apontou áreas emergentes como a computação quântica, redes de computadores e computação em nuvem como áreas que tendem a ampliar a demanda por mão de obra qualificada em todo o mundo, especialmente no Brasil.

Ele explicou que os cursos oferecidos pela Unesp na área de TI têm a missão de suprir parte dessa demanda.

"Em geral, o bacharel em ciência da computação atua com sistemas inteligentes, de automação, de comunicações e comércio eletrônico, além da área de pesquisa e desenvolvimento (P&D) em grandes empresas no Brasil e no exterior."

🧠 Não precisa ser prodígio em matemática

Rodrigo afirmou que não é necessário ser um prodígio em matemática ou programação para ingressar em ciência da computação. A grade curricular garante o conhecimento necessário para atuar na área.

"Tais conhecimentos auxiliam, mas podem perfeitamente ser adquiridos ao longo de um bom curso de graduação e mediante o esforço pessoal de cada estudante. Assim, é fundamental ter vontade de aprender, esforçar-se e dedicar-se com disciplina", acrescentou.

Apesar do curso estar em um bom momento, o professor faz um alerta aos vestibulandos que estão escolhendo qual carreira seguir.

"Devemos correr atrás dos nossos sonhos, fazendo o que gostamos. Buscar uma carreira simplesmente porque ela é a 'onda do momento' ou porque trará remuneração acima da média causará, logo adiante, frustração. Devemos buscar uma vida equilibrada em todos os sentidos (...) e crescimento como ser humano", aconselhou.

Unesp 2027: Cursos de tecnologia ganham cada vez mais espaço entre os vestibulandos — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Embora a IA seja uma área aquecida, o professor reconheceu que ela também pode impactar parte do mercado de trabalho ao substituir algumas atividades de programação por ferramentas automatizadas.

"As substituições (de programadores por ferramentas de IA) são, em geral, dos trabalhadores mais 'braçais', ou seja, os desenvolvedores de código, por exemplo. Os projetistas e engenheiros de sistemas mais elaborados não serão substituídos. Existem valores humanos que as máquinas não podem alcançar ", finalizou.

Procura pelos cursos de tecnologia na Unesp

Unesp FCLAr Araraquara. — Foto: Amanda Rocha/g1

A prova da primeira fase será aplicada no dia 22 de novembro (domingo). Os candidatos devem ficar atentos ao horário de fechamento dos portões, marcado para as 12h30.

A etapa inicial contará com 90 questões de múltipla escolha. Os exames serão aplicados em 35 municípios — 31 deles no estado de São Paulo, além das capitais Brasília (DF), Campo Grande (MS) e Curitiba (PR), e da cidade de Uberlândia (MG).

Confira as principais datas do processo seletivo:

12 de novembro: Divulgação dos locais de prova da 1ª fase no site da Vunesp;

22 de novembro: Aplicação da prova da 1ª fase (fechamento dos portões às 12h30); Após a prova, o g1 terá resolução ao vivo com professores do Colégio Oficina do Estudante.

13 e 14 de dezembro: Aplicação da 2ª fase, composta por 36 questões discursivas e uma redação dissertativa, realizada nas mesmas 35 cidades da etapa anterior;

27 de janeiro de 2027: Divulgação do resultado final.

Além do vestibular tradicional, a Unesp oferece vagas por meio de outros processos seletivos para o início de 2027:

Processo Seletivo Unesp-Enem: 726 vagas;

Olimpíadas Científicas Unesp: vagas adicionais voltadas para participantes de olimpíadas do conhecimento.

A resolução e o calendário com as regras para as vagas olímpicas e do Unesp-Enem 2027 serão divulgados em breve pela instituição. Não há impedimento para que um estudante se inscreva em mais de um processo seletivo ao mesmo tempo.

articles.title: Cratera em Divinópolis: rua desaba e moradores temem por casas | G1
articles.standfirst: Erosão na Rua Martin Cyprien, entre os bairros Belvedere e Bela Vista, em Divinópolis, impede moradores de entrar com carros nas garagens e ameaça imóveis. Vídeo mostra parte do terreno desabando durante chuva.
articles.summary: A cratera em Divinópolis na Rua Martin Cyprien impede o acesso a garagens e causa rachaduras em casas, com obras da Copasa previstas para terminar apenas em 2027.
articles.body:
Uma cratera que engoliu parte da rua Martin Cyprien, entre os bairros Belvedere e Bela Vista, em Divinópolis , tem preocupado moradores da região. A erosão, próxima ao Córrego Olhos D'Água, corta a rua e avança em direção às casas. Segundo os moradores, o problema impede a entrada de carros nas garagens e algumas residências já apresentam trincas e rachaduras nas paredes e no piso .

No início desta semana, a TV Integração esteve no local e mostrou a dimensão dos estragos (assista acima) . O trecho está sinalizado com cavaletes, mas a situação preocupa quem vive na região, principalmente com a chegada das chuvas.

A Prefeitura de Divinópolis informou que notificou a Companhia de Saneamento de Minas Gerais ( Copasa ), em caráter de urgência, cobrando providências para conter a erosão. Segundo o Município, o problema já provoca desmoronamento de solo e ameaça atingir o pavimento e imóveis próximos, colocando em risco moradores e pedestres.

Após vistorias da Defesa Civil, a Prefeitura pediu a adoção de medidas emergenciais de segurança, além de uma solução definitiva para estabilizar o terreno.

De acordo com a Copasa, as obras para conter a erosão começaram em outubro e devem ser concluídas até o fim de janeiro de 2027. Entenda mais ao fim da reportagem .

Moradora da rua Martin Cyprien há dez anos, Tatiane Cristina Fernandes viu a situação piorar desde outubro. A erosão mudou a rotina da família, que já não consegue guardar o carro na garagem e convive com rachaduras e trincas dentro de casa.

"A gente não pode mais entrar com o carro na garagem, as nossas casas estão com rachaduras, trincados, quando entram com a máquina no córrego, a nossa casa treme tudo", contou.

Vídeos enviados por Tatiane ao g1 mostram as rachaduras e trincas nas paredes e no piso da residência (veja abaixo) . A movimentação das máquinas utilizadas nas obras também preocupa a família devido aos tremores no imóvel.

Além dos transtornos dentro de casa, o avanço da cratera também mudou a rotina das crianças, que deixaram de brincar na rua por causa do perigo.

"Meus filhos não brincam na rua, fica perigoso porque se cair uma criança aqui dentro, quebra o braço ou acontece algo pior", afirmou Ederson Resende dos Santos, marido de Tatiane.

A preocupação dos moradores aumenta nos dias de chuva. Em um vídeo gravado durante um temporal, é possível ver a força da água que passa pela cratera e o momento em que parte do terreno desaba . Assista abaixo .

Para quem vive próximo à erosão, a possibilidade de novos desmoronamentos provoca medo sempre que o tempo começa a fechar.

"Quando o tempo começa a fechar, a gente vê que vai chover, começa a ter as nuvens pesadas, a gente começa a ficar apreensivo, com medo, sabe que vem chuva e o risco de desabamento é muito grande", disse Tatiane.

Em nota à TV Integração , a Copasa informou que a erosão foi provocada pelo volume de água da chuva que escoa pelo local . As redes de água e esgoto também foram afetadas, o que exige uma intervenção de alta complexidade técnica.

As obras de contenção começaram em 10 de outubro de 2026, com previsão de conclusão até o fim de janeiro de 2027. Segundo a companhia, as equipes trabalham na construção de estruturas para estabilizar o terreno e impedir o avanço da erosão.

articles.title: Família Kennedy tenta impedir Arco do Triunfo de Trump que faria sombra sobre túmulos | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto prevê estrutura de 76 metros entre o Lincoln Memorial e o Cemitério Nacional de Arlington; nove integrantes da família recorreram à Justiça.
articles.summary: Projeto prevê estrutura de 76 metros entre o Lincoln Memorial e o Cemitério Nacional de Arlington; nove integrantes da família recorreram à Justiça.
articles.body:
Uma maquete do arco do triunfo proposto pelo presidente Donald Trump é exibida na Great American State Fair, no National Mall, em Washington. — Foto: Jen Golbeck/AP

Nove integrantes da dinastia política Kennedy pediram nesta terça-feira a uma juíza que impeça o plano do presidente Donald Trump de construir um imponente arco memorial de 250 pés (76 metros) de altura. Segundo eles, a estrutura projetaria uma sombra sobre os túmulos de seus parentes no Cemitério Nacional de Arlington.

A sombra “alteraria profundamente a experiência de visitar os túmulos”, argumentaram os parentes. Eles apresentaram um pedido para participar de duas ações judiciais já existentes que buscam impedir a construção do arco.

Na semana passada, a juíza federal Tanya Chutkan proibiu o governo Trump de iniciar as obras da estrutura por 14 dias.

Os nove integrantes da família Kennedy que recorreram à Justiça são filhos e netos de Robert F. Kennedy e Edward M. Kennedy, irmãos do presidente americano assassinado John F. Kennedy. Ambos foram senadores dos Estados Unidos.

Eles estão enterrados perto da chama eterna que marca o túmulo de JFK. Os três memoriais são uma grande atração para os milhões de pessoas que visitam o Cemitério de Arlington todos os anos.

A construção do arco representaria uma “desvalorização permanente” dos túmulos, e os descendentes dos Kennedy “nunca mais poderiam apreciar os dois locais como sempre fizeram e como a família Kennedy sempre desejou”, escreveram os advogados dos parentes. Eles são representados pelo veterano advogado de Washington Norm Eisen e pelo Democracy Defenders Fund.

“É lamentável ver que alguns integrantes da família Kennedy aderiram à ação contra o Arco, já que o projeto pretende homenagear nossos heróis que descansam no Cemitério de Arlington”, afirmou o porta-voz da Casa Branca, Davis Ingle.

“O Judiciário não deve ser usado indevidamente para politizar uma estrutura concebida para unir nossa nação.”

Robert F. Kennedy Jr., secretário de Saúde e Serviços Humanos de Trump, que mantém uma relação conturbada com muitos de seus parentes, não aderiu à ação.

O arco é um dos vários projetos que o presidente republicano vem promovendo em Washington enquanto transforma a capital de acordo com suas preferências, desde a reforma de um de seus tradicionais campos de golfe públicos até a ameaça de demolir o Centro John F. Kennedy de Artes Cênicas. Esses projetos poderão enfrentar forte escrutínio em breve, depois que os democratas assumiram o controle do Congresso nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato.

Na semana passada, a Casa Branca lançou um novo e sofisticado site para apresentar o arco, que deverá ser erguido com uma profusão de ornamentos dourados e granito cinza imponente entre o Lincoln Memorial e o Cemitério Nacional de Arlington.

articles.title: Cachorro que furtava ração no RS agora aguarda atendimento no caixa | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal tem dono, mas visita estabelecimento diariamente em Arroio do Sal. Vídeos das ações do cão já ultrapassam um milhão de visualizações nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Cachorro que furtava ração em Arroio do Sal viralizou ao mudar de tática e agora late no balcão da agropecuária para exigir que sua comida seja servida na hora.
articles.body:
O cachorro que viralizou ao levar pacotes de ração de uma agropecuária em Arroio do Sal , no Litoral Norte do Rio Grande do Sul, mudou de estratégia e agora exige a comida diretamente no balcão da loja . A nova tática do animal foi detalhada pela administração do estabelecimento.

"Antes, entrava e saía com a mercadoria. Agora, vai direto ao caixa, late, acompanha a equipe e aguarda seu atendimento" , relatou a equipe da loja ao descrever a evolução do comportamento do cão, que deixou de fugir com os produtos.

O objetivo final da operação é o comedouro fixo mantido pelo estabelecimento para alimentar animais de rua. Segundo a agropecuária, o cachorro tem dono, mas visita o local diariamente para variar a alimentação e exige que a comida seja servida na hora.

"Quando ele chega, entra na loja e fica acoando até a gente servir ração nova no comedouro. Se contar, não dá pra acreditar', afirmou a administração.

A equipe define o visitante como um "bichinho muito inteligente", mas ressalta que ele "às vezes não gosta de esperar".

A postura atual de pedir no balcão contrasta com os primeiros registros feitos pelas câmeras de segurança em outubro. Antes de aprender a aguardar pelos funcionários, o cão chegou a levar dois sacos de ração de uma só vez, ação que a loja classificou com humor como um "furto qualificado".

articles.title: Nvidia hires top US law firm to investigate affair between CEO Jensen Huang and Chinese spy
articles.summary: Nvidia on Tuesday said it hired a prominent US law firm to investigate allegations surrounding a relationship between its chief executive Jensen Huang and
articles.body: Nvidia on Tuesday said it hired a prominent US law firm to investigate allegations surrounding a relationship between its chief executive Jensen Huang and a woman accused of spying for China, as the matter draws scrutiny from US lawmakers and the FBI.The company said that New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz (WLRK) would lead the inquiry, with attorney Joon Kim overseeing what it described as a “thorough and independent investigation”, BBC reported.The FBI is conducting a separate probe.Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, has acknowledged having a romantic relationship outside his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is alleged to be a Chinese spy. She is not related to the Nvidia chief.The company's shares have fallen close to a one-year low, wiping about $500 billion (£375 billion) off its market value since Friday.Nvidia is a major player in the artificial intelligence (AI) boom and the world's second most valuable company after Apple. Its chips are central to the development of AI tools and have become a national security concern for US officials seeking to maintain an edge over China in the technology race.Alice Huang was an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that has been a customer of Nvidia. Megaspeed had faced suspicions of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, but Nvidia has said it investigated the concern and found the allegations to be unfounded.The company has also maintained that the US government did not tell it that Megaspeed was an intelligence concern.According to the New York Times, US secretary of state Marco Rubio sent a memo to senior officials in Washington earlier this year warning that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.Meanwhile, China has rejected the allegations. Its foreign ministry said the claims were “intended to smear and malign China”.US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he had spoken to Huang, who told him he had “no idea she was a spy”. Trump said he believed the Nvidia chief.The matter has also reached Capitol Hill. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing next week, a person familiar with the request told the BBC.Huang has not yet indicated whether he will appear. The committee has the power to subpoena him if it decides his attendance is necessary.When Nvidia's board announced the investigation on Sunday, it said there was no reason to believe the company's trade secrets or national security had been compromised. It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the inquiry.It remains unclear whether Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, BBC reported.Wachtell is among the largest law firms in the US and counts technology companies, including OpenAI and Salesforce, among its clients. Kim, who will lead the investigation, is a former US attorney for the Southern District of New York and has worked as a government lawyer on fraud and other criminal cases.You use AI every day. However, US officials have assessed that Iran's ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the United States and other overseas territories is limited, even as they take specific threats against individuals seriously.A Treasury Department spokesperson said Bessent “will not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats”, adding that he remained committed to carrying out the administration's campaign to put pressure on Iran.Bessent at centre of US economic pressure campaign against IranBessent has led Washington's economic pressure campaign against Tehran since August, seeking to isolate Iran financially through tougher sanctions and restrictions on trade routes.The campaign aims to cut off funding to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's most powerful military force, which also controls a substantial part of the country's economy, according to The New York Times.The Treasury Department has imposed financial restrictions targeting individuals, companies, maritime networks and participants in Iran's oil trade as part of the broader effort to restrict Tehran's revenue and its ability to finance military operations.The campaign has been pursued alongside the US-Israeli military offensive against Iran, which began on February 28.Strikes by the US and Israel on Iran, along with Israeli attacks in Lebanon, have killed thousands and displaced millions across the region.The attacks have also killed several senior Iranian officials, including former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.The Trump administration hopes the economic pressure will help avoid a resumption of major military operations in the conflict, which President Donald Trump has repeatedly promised to bring to an end.Bessent and other US officials have said the campaign is hurting Iran's economy, weakening its currency and worsening living standards.However, US intelligence indicates that Iran's hard-line leadership remains determined to retain power despite the economic pressure, according to two officials cited in the report.Other Trump administration officials have also relocatedBessent is the latest senior Trump administration official to move from a private residence in linked to Iran.In Bondi's case, the threats were said to have increased partly after US forces captured former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in Caracas and brought him to New York to face federal criminal charges.Last month, the US government placed employees across the Middle East on heightened alert and reduced staffing at some embassies and consulates after receiving intelligence that Iran was at an advanced stage of planning attacks against Americans.The US military also abruptly moved bombers from a base in the United Kingdom following a suspected terrorist plot against the articles.title: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
articles.summary: Authorities struggling to contain DRC’s largest Ebola outbreak due to delayed detection and conflict.
articles.body:
The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 11,042, according to government data, with at least 5,387 deaths.

The figures, released on Tuesday, came as health authorities in the DRC struggle to contain the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history.

The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.

It is now the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind only the 2014-2016 West African outbreak. That epidemic infected more than 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000.

Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected in the ongoing outbreak, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centres.

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have led to a more rapid spread of the virus than in previous outbreaks.

Containment has been especially difficult because no vaccine or treatment has been developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, which kills about half of the people it infects.

Earlier this month, the World Health Organization approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines and said it expected results in early 2027.

Cases have now been reported in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

articles.title: Yemeni forces, Houthis exchange attacks, claim to inflict heavy losses
articles.summary: Yemen’s government says 190 rebel fighters killed and wounded, as Houthis also claim dealing heavy blows.
articles.body:
Fighting continues to rage in Yemen, with forces aligned with the country’s internationally recognised government claiming to have killed and wounded at least 190 Houthi fighters in hundreds of air and artillery attacks.

Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili, a spokesman for Yemen’s government forces, said on Tuesday that the attacks targeted Houthi positions in Lahij, Taiz, Marib, al-Jawf, Hajjah and al-Bayda governorates.

In a statement, he said Yemeni government forces carried out at least 29 air strikes and 39 drone attacks. They also fired 62 rockets and carried out 744 artillery attacks, he added.

“Initial field reports indicate that about 190 Houthi commanders and fighters were killed or injured,” al-Nuzaili said. Up to 130 vehicles and combat assets used by the Iran-allied group were damaged or destroyed, he said.

Al Jazeera could not verify the battlefield claims.

The fighting in Yemen comes amid regional tensions triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia, has launched a counteroffensive, dubbed Operation Dawn of Yemen, to retake territory lost to the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), in September. The Saudi-led coalition has supported the government’s ground campaign with air strikes, and the Houthis have fired missiles at the kingdom, targeting airports and oil facilities.

According to the World Health Organization, at least 1,771 people have been killed in the hostilities in Yemen since August, with at least 7,959 wounded. More than 300,000 people have also been displaced.

The Houthis said on Tuesday that Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces launched 109 air strikes and missile attacks on the rebel-controlled capital, Sanaa, as well as on Houthi positions in al-Jawf, Saada, Taiz, Lahij and Marib.

Yahya Saree, the Houthi spokesman, said the attacks killed and wounded “a large number of women and children”.

Separately, Saree also claimed the Houthis killed and wounded “a large number” of government-aligned fighters in attacks on al-Madaribah and Ras al-Ara areas in the Lahij governorate on Tuesday.

He said dozens more government soldiers were killed and wounded in attacks on al-Jawf earlier in the day.

Saree added that the Houthis also targeted the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and an Aramco oil facility in Abqaiq in the kingdom’s Eastern province.

Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two missiles fired by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh, and another aimed at its southern region.

articles.title: Duck attacker exposes bottom to patrol volunteer at Dorset river
articles.summary: The three men were seen throwing objects at the ducks before the patrol volunteer stopped them.
articles.body:
Three people seen attacking ducks in Dorset exposed their bottoms to a duck patrol volunteer after they were confronted, the BBC has been told.

The woman said she heard a duck in distress near the River Frome in Dorchester at 15:25 on Sunday and found the men throwing objects at the birds.

When she shouted at the group to stop, they turned towards her and exposed their bottoms before running away.

Dorset Police said officers from the local neighbourhood policing team were aware of the incident and would be carrying out inquiries.

The witness told the BBC: "I followed them with my phone on video mode, hoping to get a picture of their faces.

"They were walking away from me at speed up Friary Hill. I kept walking after them and then they turned around and jeered at me and said something."

After the group fled, she said her main concern was checking if the ducks had been injured.

"I could have rescued them and taken them to the vets, but they seemed to be all okay," she said.

More than half a dozen attacks on ducks have been reported in the area so far this year, with several birds found injured or dead.

The incidents prompted resident Gillian May to establish the Dorchester Duck Patrol in the spring in an effort to protect the wildlife and prevent further attacks.

She was not the woman involved in the incident on Sunday.

A Dorset Police spokesperson said: "Anti-social behaviour and cruelty towards animals will not be tolerated and regular patrols of the area will continue.

articles.title: Bid to restore rare Atlantic rainforest secures £6m lottery grant
articles.summary: Hubs offering training in conservation work are to be set up in Torridon, Morvern and mid-Argyll.
articles.body:
Almost £6m has been given to a five-year project set up to restore Scotland's rare rainforest.

The award from the National Lottery Heritage Fund will support the creation of three hubs to be located in Torridon, Morvern and mid-Argyll.

Through the Our Rainforest Futures project local people will be given training and work opportunities around habitat restoration, deer management and the removal of invasive species.

About 75,000 acres (30,351ha) of rain-soaked woodlands on the west coast are designated Atlantic rainforest because of the rare oceanic plant life.

Rare species found in Scotland's declining rainforest

When Amazon leaders blessed Scotland's rainforest

The forest has been found to be home to hundreds of species including glow worms, slime moulds and rare lichens.

Overgrazing by deer and livestock, invasive plant species and disease are among the threats to the surviving areas of woodland.

The Torridon hub would involve communities in Kinlochewe, Shieldaig, Lochcarron, Applecross and Gairloch.

In Morvern, the project would include Lochaline, Strontian and Tobermory in Mull.

Mid-Argyll's hub would involve communities Crinan, Tayvallich, Lochgilphead, Ardrishaig and Tarbert.

Our Rainforest Futures is an Alliance for Scotland's Rainforest project led by the Woodland Trust Scotland.

Argyll Countryside Trust, Community Woodlands Association, Plantlife, RSPB Scotland and SRUC are involved.

Caroline Clark, Scotland director of The National Lottery Heritage Fund, said Scotland's rainforest was internationally significant but largely unknown.

She said: "A 2025 survey found fewer than one in three people even know it exists.

"This major investment, using funds raised by National Lottery players, recognises that the future of our rainforest and the future of many west coast communities are closely linked. With the right support, both can thrive."

Julie Stoneman, Saving Scotland's Rainforest Programme manager at the charity Plantlife, said it was hoped the project could create more than 20 jobs and 15 trainee posts.

articles.title: If hackers can take over a supermarket fridge, what else is at risk?
articles.summary: As our lives become more digitised, we show which smart systems can be hacked and how to protect yourself.
articles.body:
Hackers have twice taken control of supermarket fridges across Europe in less than a month, sparking fires and spoiling millions of euros’ worth of food.

On October 11 and 12, attackers heated units at about 700 French stores to as high as 50C (122F). On November 2, a second wave of suspected cyberattacks affected supermarkets and food businesses in at least nine European countries, including Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden.

France has since blamed the first attack on Shahid Kaveh , a cyberunit affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), calling it the first large-scale sabotage cyberattack on French soil. It is not yet clear who was behind the second wave.

The attacks have raised concern about how exposed internet-connected equipment has become, from industrial machinery to household appliances. Al Jazeera illustrates the devices at risk in your home and the essential services you rely on, and what you can do to protect yourself.

A supermarket’s fridges and freezers are run from one control panel, which is connected to the internet so contractors can manage it remotely. Home smart fridges connect the same way, through Wi-Fi, an app or a cloud service.

The attackers reportedly found the supermarket systems using Shodan, a search engine for internet-connected devices. According to Vincent Strubel, head of France’s National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI), they got in through basic security failures:

Exposed : The equipment was directly connected to the open internet with no extra protection.

Weak passwords : Many systems were protected only by weak or default logins.

Outdated : Many units were old models that no longer get security updates.

Once inside, hackers can switch a fridge off, raise its temperature or steal account details. In France, they simply used the controllers’ own defrost function. A poorly protected fridge can also be a doorway to other devices on the same network, from laptops to smart locks.

Speaking to the French Senate on October 21, Strubel warned that the healthcare sector uses the same type of equipment to store vaccines and hazardous materials, from research laboratories to pharmacies.

Essentially, anything connected via the internet could potentially be hacked.

There are about 21 billion short-range connected devices, such as smartwatches, worldwide and 5.4 billion long-range ones, such as remote monitoring systems, according to Kepios’s Digital 2027 Global Overview Report. US internet households now have an average of about 18 connected devices, nearly double the number a decade ago, according to Parks Associates.

Routers are among the biggest targets because they are always online. In April , the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned that hackers linked to Russia’s GRU military intelligence were hijacking home and small business routers. By tampering with their DNS settings, which turn website names into IP addresses, the hackers redirected users to fake websites to steal passwords and personal details.

Smart TVs can be hacked without their owners knowing. In June, researchers found that more than a third of apps on LG and Samsung smart TVs could let strangers secretly use a household’s internet connection , hiding their own activity behind that home’s IP address.

Robot vacuums can expose even more. Earlier this year, a programmer reportedly found he could control almost 7,000 DJI Romo robot vacuums with a PlayStation 5 controller. Using Claude Code, an AI coding tool made by Anthropic, to work out how the vacuums talked to DJI’s servers, he gained access to their live camera feeds, audio and floor plans of people’s homes.

The same weaknesses that expose a fridge can affect power plants, water supplies, banks and hospitals.

Many of these services are run by industrial computers that can be reached online. Since the US-Israel war on Iran began, US agencies have warned that Iran-affiliated hackers are attacking these systems.

In July, a cyberattack in the US state of Minnesota targeted more than 30 community water systems, according to the state’s IT agency. Officials suspected Iran-aligned hackers, and the FBI and CISA warned that water and wastewater systems were increasingly being targeted, with facilities in 12 states affected at the time.

That same month, a cyberattack attributed to Iran-linked hackers forced a small British power plant offline for four days. It was reported as the first successful attack of its kind on UK energy infrastructure.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) lists sectors it considers critical infrastructure. The graphic below shows some of the key ones, and what a hack on each could mean for you.

Banks are targets, too. In late September and early October, hackers stole personal data from at least seven South Korean financial firms, affecting about 68,000 people. Yegaram Savings Bank and Shinhan Bank were hit hardest, with about 40,000 and 25,000 customers affected, respectively.

According to The Wall Street Journal, the attacker used ARTEX, an open-source AI tool developed in China to test networks for weaknesses. US cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike said the attacker was likely a China-based individual who also used Claude Code, an assessment it made with moderate confidence.

Which industries are most politically targeted?

The European Repository of Cyber Incidents (EuRepoC), a research database tracking political cyberattacks worldwide, logged 4,932 major incidents between January 2000 and November 2026.

The number of incidents has grown sharply in recent years, peaking at 795 in 2024. About two-thirds of all incidents recorded since 2000 have occurred since 2022.

Governments are the biggest target. State institutions account for nearly 40 percent of all targets, led by the civil service and government ministries, followed by the military, police, political parties and legislatures.

Critical infrastructure is the second most targeted sector, led by health, finance, telecommunications, transport and energy, followed by defence firms, manufacturing, research and digital service providers. Companies, schools, civil society groups and media outlets make up most of the rest.

EuRepoC tracks only politically significant attacks, a fraction of all cyberattacks. Beyond these, hackers often target individuals and companies with scams.

Hackers rely on weaknesses such as weak passwords and devices that no longer receive updates.

Awais Rashid, a professor of cybersecurity at the University of Bristol, told Al Jazeera that as infrastructure becomes more digitised, the risk of disruption from cyberattacks has risen. But, he added, “the world works because cybersecurity works effectively”.

The UK’s NCSC also advises people to turn off features they don’t use, such as remote camera access.

If a power plant or water system is hacked, there is little individuals can do. The UK’s Be Ready campaign, launched last month partly in response to cyber-threats, urges households to keep a three-day supply of water, food, medicine, cash and torches.

articles.title: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia
articles.summary: US general warns the Sahel model-like security deal with Russia could lead to greater instability in Africa.
articles.body:
The US has warned Madagascar against strengthening its ties with Russia, saying similar partnerships with military-led governments in West Africa have failed to improve security.

US Africa Command deputy head Lt Gen John Brennan said Madagascar's strategic location in the Indian Ocean made it important to global trade.

He warned against what he called the "Sahel model", which he said risked fuelling instability across the continent.

Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, all under military rule, have severed ties with the Western partners and turned to Russia to military support their fight against jihadist groups.

Russia has expanded its military cooperation with Madagascar since the military seized power in 2025, supplying weapons and military instructors.

"We are concerned about Russia wanting to "proliferate [the Sahel model] elsewhere across the continent", Brennan told reporters in an online briefing.

"Madagascar sits in a location that is extremely important, as is Mozambique, and we don't want to see those models be applied in those two locations," he said.

The three Sahel countries had blamed their former Western partners for failing to contain jihadist violence before turning to Moscow.

However, militant attacks have continued despite their closer military ties with Russia.

Brennan also raised concerns about security in the Mozambique Channel, which separates Mozambique and Madagascar from mainland Africa and is an important route for international shipping and trade.

He said it was vital to prevent Islamist State linked militants in northern Mozambique and other hostile actors from threatening maritime activity.

Citing recent piracy-related incidents along the coast, Brennan said militant groups in northern Mozambique were adapting their tactics, including developing greater maritime capabilities.

He said US partners were "free to partner with whom they wish" but urged them to understand the potential risks.

Madagascar has not publicly responded to Brennan's comments,.

However, President Michaël Randrianirina has recently reiterated his support for stronger ties between Russia and African countries.

During the Russia-Africa summit last month, Madagascar and Russia signed several cooperation agreements covering defence, tourism and trade.

In February, a few months after taking power in a military takeover, Randrianirina visited to Moscow. It was the first official visit to Russia by a Malagasy leader in nearly 50 years.

articles.summary: A suspect was working at a Miami Beach Burger King when local police and U.S. Marshals arrested him over three alleged rapes reported in Central Park.
articles.body: A man suspected in three sexual assaults spanning five years in New York City's Central Park was arrested Tuesday at a Burger King in Miami Beach, Florida, authorities said. Dereck Rivera-Deleon, 30, was taken into custody during an operation involving the NYPD, U.S. Marshals Service and Miami Beach police at a fast-food restaurant in the 1100 block of Washington Avenue. "The NYPD will stop at nothing to get dangerous criminals off our streets," police said on X. DEMS SILENT AFTER VIOLENT ATTACK IN WEALTHY AREA OF NEW YORK CITY AS SUSPECT REMAINS AT LARGE Investigators located Rivera-Deleon in South Florida, where he had recently arrived and obtained employment at the restaurant, according to authorities. The arrest followed an investigation into an Oct. 24 rape reported near Central Park's eastern edge in Manhattan. An extraditable warrant was issued Monday in connection with the Oct. 24 assault. Police said the attack happened at about 8:30 p.m. that night, when officers responded to a report of an assault near East 66th Street and Fifth Avenue. The 39-year-old victim told investigators she was approached by a man who threatened her with a knife, forced her into a wooded section of the park and raped her before fleeing, according to police. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani previously described the attack as a "horrific" act. Investigators also connected Rivera-Deleon to alleged sexual assaults in Central Park in 2021 and 2023 through DNA evidence and victim identifications, according to Miami Beach police. Authorities said he is expected to face charges in connection with both earlier incidents. articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) will set up five additional continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations (CAQMS) across Mumbai
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) will set up five additional continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations (CAQMS) across Mumbai at a cost of Rs 17.50 crore.The five monitoring stations will be set up at CD Deshmukh Garden in Mulund (East), Pramod Mahajan Park in Borivali (West), Aarey Garden's Chhota Kashmir in Goregaon (East), Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Recreation Ground in Dahisar (East), and the BMC assistant municipal commissioner's office in Khar (H-West ward).The proposed stations will monitor various air pollutants on an hourly basis and measure meteorological parameters such as temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and direction.The data is proposed to be made available on the BMC portal, which will be linked to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) server.Mumbai currently has 28 air quality monitoring stations.The civic body said the five new stations would be located in areas not already covered by monitoring networks operated by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), BMC and the SAFAR-Mumbai project.The project will include a three-year warranty and five years of subsequent maintenance. articles.title: Why Do Opposite Zodiac Signs Attract Each Other? The Astrology Behind 6 Unusual Love Matches
articles.summary: Look at any zodiac wheel and draw a straight line through the middle. The two signs at either end are opposites, and they have a reputation.
articles.body: Look at any zodiac wheel and draw a straight line through the middle. The two signs at either end are opposites, and they have a reputation. Friends warn against these pairings. Compatibility charts give them low scores. And yet a surprising number of long marriages turn out to be exactly this kind of match.So what is going on?Opposites Have More in Common Than It SeemsThe first clue is in the pace. Opposite signs always share the same quality. Cardinal signs pair with cardinal signs, fixed with fixed, mutable with mutable. Two people who move through life at a similar speed tend to find each other easy company, even when their goals look very different.Elements help as well. Fire always sits across from Air, and Earth across from Water. These elements feed each other in astrology. Air keeps a fire going. Water softens dry ground.Then there is the seventh house. In a natal chart, it describes partners and the kind of person someone is drawn to marry. For many people, the sign on that house is the one opposite their rising sign. Astrologers read it as the missing half. It shows qualities a person does not show easily and secretly admires in someone else.Aries and LibraAries rarely waits for permission. Libra can spend twenty minutes choosing a restaurant. It sounds like a recipe for irritation, and some days it is. But Aries gives Libra a push to finally decide something. Libra, in return, teaches Aries that other people have feelings worth checking first. Mars and Venus rule these two signs, which explains a lot about the chemistry.Taurus and ScorpioThis one runs deep. Both signs are loyal to the point of being possessive. Taurus wants a calm home and a full fridge. Scorpio wants total honesty, every hidden detail. Arguments between them can stretch across a whole week because neither likes to give in first. Still, once trust is settled, this couple is very hard to break apart.Gemini and SagittariusPlenty of talking here. Gemini picks up a new topic every hour, and Sagittarius is happy to turn each one into a debate about life. They share a love of travel too. The weak spot is daily routine. Someone has to book the dentist appointment, and neither is keen to volunteer.Cancer and CapricornCancer is the Moon’s sign and Capricorn belongs to Saturn. One looks after feelings. The other looks after the long-term plan, the savings account, the five-year goal. Early on, Cancer may find Capricorn cold. Over time that changes. Many astrologers count this among the opposite pairs that improve the longer it lasts.Leo and AquariusLeo likes attention and makes no secret of it. Aquarius cares about the wider group and can seem distant in private. So there will be a few awkward evenings. But Aquarius often admires Leo’s warmth more than it admits. And Leo learns from Aquarius that a friendship-based love can be just as strong as a dramatic one.Virgo and PiscesA Virgo notices the tap that drips. A Pisces may not notice it for a month. That gap causes some friction, naturally. Yet Pisces brings kindness and patience into Virgo’s busy, list-driven world. Virgo gives Pisces something solid to lean on when plans fall through, like a cancelled train on a rainy morning.Looking Beyond the Sun SignSun signs only show a slice of the picture. A couple with opposite Suns may have Moons in the same element, which makes home life far smoother. Venus placements matter for affection. Mars shows how each person handles anger. A full synastry reading, comparing both charts side by side, gives a much clearer answer than the Sun pairing alone.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Stories of life, death – and crows – from ‘The Forgotten War’
articles.summary: Patrick Finn, a 95-year-old Korean War veteran, watches from a wheelchair as a staff member uses a pencil to rub the name “Edmund Hubert Reilly” from the Wall of the Fallen onto a piece of paper.
articles.body: Patrick Finn, a 95-year-old Korean War veteran, watches from a wheelchair as a staff member uses a pencil to rub the name “Edmund Hubert Reilly” from the Wall of the Fallen onto a piece of paper. US military archives call the Korean War “The Forgotten War,” though some 1.8 million Americans served during its three years – and more than 36,500 of them died, along with at least 200,000 South Korean, 400,000 North Korean and 600,000 Chinese troops. But Finn, who fought in one of the war’s bloodiest battles, has never forgotten the Marine from Center Point, Iowa, who saved his life twice. He will carry his name back home to Minnesota. Reilly came to Finn’s rescue twice on the icy battlefield of the Chosin Reservoir in late 1950, Finn says, once by pushing him to dig his foxhole deeper into the frozen ground. “It was just like digging into concrete, but we did. And luckily, because it wasn’t long after we got settled in there, a mortar hit and if we had been any shallower, we would’ve been killed,” Finn says. The second occasion also had to do with the cold, with temperatures as low as –35 degrees Fahrenheit (–37 degrees Celsius.) “We were completely surrounded,” says Finn, who was a Marine reservist before the war. “I realized there was a Chinese soldier right to my left. So, I quickly rolled around to shoot him, and my gun just clicked. It was frozen.” But his fellow Marine was there. Reilly “shot him for me… He was my guardian angel.” Reilly would be killed a few days later. “December 3rd, I think it was,” says Finn, who was just 19 years old at the time. “He came into my life and he left … (and) saved it twice.” Koreans haven’t forgotten If the war is forgotten in the US, Finn is adamant that in South Korea, it isn’t. And his presence in Seoul – a modern megacity unrecognizable from the 1950s – proves it. He’s one of some 60 US veterans and their escorts invited by the Korean Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs (KMPVA) on an all-expenses-paid trip to Korea as a thank you for their service – trips that happen four or five times a year. On the final night of the September trip, Finn watches as a slight Korean man, Sohn Yang-young, rises to give a speech to a packed ballroom in the Ambassador Hotel in Seoul. Sohn is one of the so-called Kimchi babies, born to refugees aboard a cargo ship, the SS Meredith Victory, fleeing North Korea after the Chosin Reservoir battle. “I believe that without the great courage and devotion from the (United Nations Command) veterans and the captain, I would never have been able to come into this world,” Sohn says. “I will never forget your kindness.” As Finn listens, he tears up. It’s not the first time he has heard those sentiments during this trip. At a banquet the previous night, a Korean man noticed the necktie Finn wears, which bears the moniker for survivors of Chosin Reservoir: “The Chosin Few.” Finn says the man told him that his grandparents lived near the battlefield and were among the refugees evacuated in the wave that left along with the Meredith Victory. Finn and those fighting alongside him blunted the Chinese advance so the refugees could get out. “You know, you gave me my life… I wouldn’t be here if it hadn’t been for the Marines,” Finn recalls the man telling him. “And that made things so worthwhile,” Finn says. Flipping a coin, caring for crows For many on the trip, it’s their first time back. Elmore Brown, also 95, is one of them. He’s small in stature, large in presence. A blue cap, “Korea Veteran” emblazoned on it, rarely leaves his head. Brown was a logger in Oregon before the war. During his time in Korea, he was at the front in some of its bloodiest engagements. Then a sergeant, he led a team of seven men – five Americans and two Koreans – laying communications wires from the front lines back to command posts in the rear. There are things he’ll never forget, including the T-Bone battles of 1952 and ’53. China would lose thousands of men over the course of the campaign, and Brown describes the pitiless scene seven decades later. Dead Chinese troops covered the battlefield, he says, “any place you wanted to look. No, they never picked them up… when you were there, you went ahead with a gun, and when you got shot, next guy picked your gun up and went ahead.” Life or death was – at least in one instance – literally a coin flip. Brown tells the story of having to choose between two communication lines that needed to be fixed, one to a switchboard and one to a lookout. “Some guy said he had a quarter, so we flipped it and the quarter said we went towards the lookout,” Brown says. Minutes later, enemy fire rained down on the route they would’ve taken to the switchboard – a life-saving flip of 25 cents. The bonds forged during the war were not only with humans. Brown says his team found a nest with two baby crows in a fallen tree. “We didn’t want to let them starve, so we loaded them up and took them back to camp,” he says. The crows quickly became a fixture of camp life, living uncaged in the GIs’ tents for three or four months, even waking them up for food when they got hungry – not always at convenient times. “They didn’t know the time. Five o’clock in the morning,” Brown says with a smile. But the man-bird bond only goes so far. One day, a flock of birds flew over camp. The two crows rose up to join them, never looking back. “Maybe it was their folk, I don’t know.” Don’t forget my friend, Duane Dewey Ninety-three-year-old US Marine veteran John Foley is back in Korea with one key mission: To make sure his buddy Duane Dewey is not forgotten. He eagerly recounts their time together, from boot camp on Parris Island and the train ride west to Camp Pendleton in California, to mountain warfare training in the Sierra Nevada. His eyes light up with the memories. But once in Korea, the friends would be assigned to different battalions and see each other only occasionally in rear areas, Foley says. On April 16, 1952, Dewey was badly wounded when he threw his body on a grenade to shield a Navy corpsman from the blast. He would survive and eventually be evacuated for medical treatment in the States. Foley was at a different part of the front that day and would never see his friend again. Dewey died in 2021. “Today it’s so much easier to stay in touch with people or friends or family. Back then, it wasn’t… When I left the Marine Corps, I went right into the police department in New York City. I was kind of like involved in my own life,” Foley says. But Dewey is with him always. “I have a picture of him that I carry. I also have it in my phone, and I tell people because he was a really nice guy…” “I wanted to tell his story,” Foley says, his voice breaking with emotion. “I want to still, he was still my friend.” As the final banquet wraps up at the Seoul hotel, Foley scrolls through his phone, looking for that picture of Dewey. It’s a photo of a newspaper clipping from 1953. President Dwight D. Eisenhower is presenting Dewey with the US military’s highest decoration, the Medal of Honor. In the truest sense of the word, Duane Dewey was an American hero – and Jack Foley wants that to always be remembered. The accidental soldier It’s not just war veterans that the Korean government honors with trips back to the peninsula. Anyone who’s served since is eligible, too. Raul Guerrero fits that description, serving in the US Army military police in 1968, 15 years into a US-South Korean mutual defense arrangement that endures to this day. On a warm, sunny afternoon, at a park not far from the demilitarized zone that has separated North and South since 1953, he shares his story. On Halloween Day 1967, Guerrero says he and his friend dropped by a military recruiting office in El Paso, Texas, just to make some preliminary inquiries about joining up. The recruiters said they should head to nearby Fort Bliss to take an aptitude test. But upon arrival, they inadvertently got mixed in with a busload of draftees arriving for their inductions. A physical, some paperwork and an oath, and, by late afternoon, a sergeant said, “You’re in the Army now,” and the pair were off to boot camp – and, in a few months, South Korea, Guerrero says. But he never regretted a minute of it. For one, it wasn’t Vietnam (this was at the height of that conflict); and two, the Korean people embraced him. Patrolling neighborhoods of Daegu, outside a US base, Guerrero says he would be invited into Korean homes at a time when the country did not enjoy the standard of living it does today. “They gave me whatever they had: Whey, some ramen, whatever food they had,” he says. When his 12-month tour was up, he didn’t want to leave, and he asked assigners if he could remain. “Can I stay here another six months? Can I extend? Can I extend?” he recalls saying. “They said, ‘You like it that much here?’ I said, ‘Yes, I want to stay here.’” “Two weeks later, I was gone,” he laments, recalling crying on the train ride to Seoul to catch a plane to the US. Fast forward 58 years to this past September at Incheon International Airport. Guerrero emerges from the customs area to a big sign: “Welcome veterans!” “I lost it. The welcoming was so overwhelming. I actually started crying,” he says, the emotions catching him again under the afternoon sun. During Guerrero’s first time in South Korea, the country was still in the early days of its postwar modernization. Daily life was still a mix of old and new: Apartment complexes were being built among old traditional hanok houses; people were either dressed in modern-style outfits or traditional hanbok. He talks of what Korea has become in those six decades – gleaming skyscrapers, advanced technologies, even K-pop. “I feel that I’ve had some type of connection … (with) what’s going on now, that I was part of this, maybe a little small part.” “How many other American citizens came by, soldiers come by and done this, worked with this? You know, thousands, thousands of us. And it’s just beautiful. It’s just real beautiful.” The “Champion Soldier” After the KMPVA program in Seoul and the surrounding region ended, Elmore Brown and his grandson traveled south to Busan, where Brown first landed in Korea 74 years ago. The grandson, Paul Marlow, recounted that part of Brown’s journey to CNN. Brown, with the “Korea Veteran” cap still on his head, was called the “Champion Soldier” by people he met and honored at every turn, Marlow said. A taxi driver who chauffeured them around the region’s sights was 74 years old and a Busan native, “possibly an infant or was born shortly after Elmore’s arrival to Busan,” Marlow wrote, noting the implausible happenstance. The driver made sure Brown got up-close access to whatever he wanted to see – “he never took no for an answer,” Marlow says – and their hotel comped meals and lounge access. One evening at dinner, as they went to pay, they were told the bill was already taken care of. A Korean family dining nearby had wanted to show their gratitude. “Elmore was in shock at the love and kindness showed,” Marlow said. “Even outside of the official program the people and culture shined through on how proud they are to be Korean, and how grateful they are for the veterans that fought for their present-day way of life!” Marlow wrote. “After seeing how well Korea has done after the war, Elmore repeated many times that his service was indeed ‘worth it,’ that sadly the lives lost were ‘worth it,’ as it elevated the Korean people to what they have today.”

articles.title: Spain demands TikTok suspension until child abuse material is removed
articles.summary: Spain’s government has demanded that ​TikTok suspend its operations in the country until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media ⁠report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views.
articles.body: Spain’s government has demanded that ​TikTok suspend its operations in the country until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media ⁠report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views. Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has ⁠appealed to prosecutors and ​the ⁠Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to ⁠a statement by the ministry. “Social media cannot be ​lawless ⁠territory,” Rego said. The ‌request comes months after Pedro Sanchez’s government requested a probe into X, Meta and TikTok for ‌allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse ‌material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content. TikTok did not immediately respond ⁠to a Reuters request for comment. Spanish fact-checking nonprofit Maldita.es on Monday published an investigation revealing that videos of explicit child sexual abuse had been viewed on the platform at least 48 million times, with over 26,000 profiles commenting on ‌and sharing the material. The organization published a ​follow-up story on Tuesday evening stating that ‌TikTok had restricted ⁠two of the search terms that Maldita.es’s ⁠investigation identified as pathways to child sexual abuse content for ‌users in ​Spain, but that searches from ‌other European countries ​still led to the same content.

articles.title: 'She's like a statesman': Robert Vadra urges BJP leaders to read Sonia Gandhi's memoir
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sonia Gandhi’s son-in-law and businessman Robert Vadra on Wednesday urged BJP leaders to read the Congress parliamentary party chairperson’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sonia Gandhi’s son-in-law and businessman Robert Vadra on Wednesday urged BJP leaders to read the Congress parliamentary party chairperson’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, with an “open mind”.“I would say that the BJP people should learn from Mrs Gandhi. I would say that they should read the book with an open mind. She's like a statesman and she's like a mentor to many people,” Vadra said, speaking to news agency ANI.Vadra said he was proud of his mother-in-law and the experiences she had shared in the book, which he received from her on Tuesday. He said he was yet to read the memoir but intended to do so.“I'm very proud of my mother-in-law for her life, her experience, my relationship with her, what I've learned from her, how she takes care of everything. And definitely all of that and more is in the book. Though I'll say that I still haven't read the book, but I'm a proud owner of the book which I received yesterday from her,” he said.Vadra also revealed that Sonia Gandhi had personally dedicated the book to him.“She mentioned she wrote a little something for me, that 'to my son-in-law Robert with lots of love, your mom-in-law'.”“So it's a personal book for me which I'm going to definitely read,” he said.He said the memoir took 12 years to complete and drew on her real-life experiences. Vadra described her as a woman who had shown strength and resilience while dealing with difficulties and making important decisions.“She's always had a lot of strength, resilience and energy to deal with everything every day,” he said.Referring to her move to India after marrying into the Gandhi family, Vadra said she had shown considerable commitment and strength.“She's a strong, sincere lady with a lot of experience, a lot of commitment that she learned when she gave up her life and she got married and came to this country. And coming to the Gandhi family requires a lot of strength,” he said.Vadra also recalled Sonia Gandhi's support during his questioning by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Alleging that he had faced false accusations and repeated summons, he said she would wait for him after each interrogation to check on his well-being.“Every time I returned from my interrogation, I saw my mother-in-law was there waiting for me to see how I'm doing. Her experience really helped, and it gave me the strength to deal with anything which was even false that I had to deal with,” he said.Defending Sonia Gandhi's decision to decline the prime minister's post after the 2004 Lok Sabha elections, Vadra said she was not seeking political power. He described her decision to nominate Manmohan Singh for the post as “a very wise decision”.He said people respected her for not pursuing positions and for wanting the country to remain secular and develop as a society.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
